craft_claim: Nostalgia is normally reached from a present lack - loneliness, rupture, meaning threat - or from a sensory reminder that opens the past unbidden. The tone therefore needs a present-tense deficit (or a concrete trigger) on the page; longing with no current lack reads as decoration.

supporting_evidence.location: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology 91(5):975-993, Study 4 and trigger analyses
supporting_evidence.note: An induced loneliness state increased nostalgia (Study 4), and self-reported triggers cluster around sad, poignant, lonely moments and sensorial reminders - the emotion reaches toward the past when the present hurts or lacks.

supporting_evidence.location: European Journal of Social Psychology 45(1):52-61, Studies 1-2
supporting_evidence.note: Only negative self-discontinuity (relatively disruptive negative life events) evoked heightened nostalgia; positive discontinuity did not. The trigger is deprivation, not change as such.

supporting_evidence.location: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology 101(3):638-652, Studies 3-4
supporting_evidence.note: Threats to meaning increase nostalgia (Study 3), and nostalgia in turn reduces defensiveness following a meaning threat (Study 4); threatened meaning is a verified antecedent.

scope: Scene-level causation: why this character reaches for the past now; feeds card section 4 and failure analysis.
exceptions: Sensory triggers (taste, scent, a song) can open nostalgia without dysphoria - the deficit may be quiet or even absent in a warm, gratitude-framed register (see natsukashii, section E).
